Write a React TypeScript component FloatingOrb.tsx + FloatingOrb.css:
a hero section with a Three.js / React Three Fiber floating 3D orb.

Requirements:
- Canvas with frameloop="demand" for on-demand rendering
- DPR bounded to [1, 1.5] for laptop GPU safety
- One ambient + one directional light only (2 max)
- Animate rotation with useFrame; call invalidate() to self-sustain
- prefers-reduced-motion: pause animation, show a static orb
- WebGL unavailable: show CSS gradient circle fallback (no crash)
- Skip link above canvas for screen readers
- Warm ivory/copper MeshStandardMaterial, charcoal background, fullscreen height
- Named export FloatingOrb

Key patterns to get right: 1. frameloop=demand stops GPU overdraw when idle; invalidate() inside useFrame sustains animation. 2. Detect prefers-reduced-motion in a React useEffect (not inside useFrame) to avoid stale closures. 3. Probe WebGL availability before mounting Canvas — show CSS fallback on failure. 4. Keep geometry segments to 32 and lights to 2; SphereGeometry at 128 costs 16x more vertices with no visible benefit at this scale. 5. Export as named export, not default, so tree-shaking and fast refresh work correctly. import React, { useRef, useEffect, Suspense, useState } from 'react'; import { Canvas, useFrame, useThree } from '@react-three/fiber'; import * as THREE from 'three'; import './FloatingOrb.css'; function OrbMesh({ paused }: { paused: boolean }) { const meshRef = useRef(null); const { invalidate } = useThree(); useFrame((_state, delta) => { if (paused || !meshRef.current) return; meshRef.current.rotation.x += delta * 0.18; meshRef.current.rotation.y += delta * 0.28; invalidate(); }); return ( ); } function CSSFallback() { return (
); } export function FloatingOrb() { const [prefersReduced, setPrefersReduced] = useState(false); const [webglFailed, setWebglFailed] = useState(false); useEffect(() => { const mq = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)'); setPrefersReduced(mq.matches); const h = (e: MediaQueryListEvent) => setPrefersReduced(e.matches); mq.addEventListener('change', h); return () => mq.removeEventListener('change', h); }, []); useEffect(() => { try { const c = document.createElement('canvas'); if (!c.getContext('webgl') && !c.getContext('experimental-webgl')) setWebglFailed(true); } catch { setWebglFailed(true); } }, []); return (
Skip 3D animation {webglFailed ? : ( )}

Five distinct performance bugs: 1. dpr max=3: renders a 4K canvas on a laptop GPU. Fix: cap to [1, 1.5]. 2. frameloop defaults to 'always': GPU redraws at 60fps even when idle. Fix: frameloop=demand + invalidate(). 3. 5 lights (ambient + 4 point/spot/directional): massive specular overdraw. Fix: 2 lights max. 4. sphereGeometry 128x128 = 16,384 vertices. At this scale 32x32 is visually identical. Fix: 32x32 (97% fewer vertices). 5. castShadow not disabled: shadow maps computed by default. Fix: castShadow={false} on all lights. Bonus: useFrame delta-based rotation makes animation frame-rate independent. // AFTER — five performance issues fixed, comments explain each change import { Canvas, useFrame, useThree } from '@react-three/fiber'; import { useRef } from 'react'; import * as THREE from 'three'; import './FixedScene.css'; function Sphere() { const ref = useRef(null); const { invalidate } = useThree(); // fix 2: demand rendering useFrame((_s, delta) => { if (!ref.current) return; ref.current.rotation.y += delta * 0.6; // delta-based: frame-rate independent invalidate(); }); return ( {/* fix 4: 32x32 not 128x128 */} ); } export default function FixedScene() { return (

Write a React TypeScript component ScrollCameraHero.tsx + ScrollCameraHero.css
that moves the camera along a path as the user scrolls.

Requirements:
- Use @react-three/drei ScrollControls + useScroll
- Camera lerps (factor 0.06) from [0, 0, 8] to [0, 2, 3] as scroll goes 0→1
- Three simple box meshes at different Z depths as landmarks
- Mobile (< 768px): disable scroll controls, use static centered view
- frameloop=demand, dpr [1, 1.5], max 2 lights
- prefers-reduced-motion: freeze camera at midpoint, no scroll movement
- Named export ScrollCameraHero

Scroll-driven camera: ScrollControls wraps the scene; useScroll gives offset 0-1. lerp camera position inside useFrame using THREE.MathUtils.lerp or Vector3.lerp. On mobile: render without ScrollControls (static scene, no scroll hijacking). prefers-reduced-motion: read in React, pass as prop, freeze camera at t=0.5 (midpoint). frameloop=demand still works with ScrollControls because drei calls invalidate on scroll offset changes. import React, { useRef, useEffect, useState } from 'react'; import { Canvas, useFrame, useThree } from '@react-three/fiber'; import { ScrollControls, useScroll } from '@react-three/drei'; import * as THREE from 'three'; import './ScrollCameraHero.css'; const START = new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, 8); const END = new THREE.Vector3(0, 2, 3); function CameraRig({ paused }: { paused: boolean }) { const { camera, invalidate } = useThree(); const scroll = useScroll(); const target = useRef(START.clone()); useFrame(() => { const t = paused ? 0.5 : scroll.offset; target.current.lerpVectors(START, END, t); camera.position.lerp(target.current, 0.06); camera.lookAt(0, 0, 0); invalidate(); }); return null; } function Landmarks() { return ( <> ); } function Lights() { return ( <> ); } export function ScrollCameraHero() { const [isMobile, setIsMobile] = useState(false); const [prefersReduced, setPrefersReduced] = useState(false); useEffect(() => { const mq = window.matchMedia('(max-width: 767px)'); const rm = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)'); setIsMobile(mq.matches); setPrefersReduced(rm.matches); const onMQ = (e: MediaQueryListEvent) => setIsMobile(e.matches); const onRM = (e: MediaQueryListEvent) => setPrefersReduced(e.matches); mq.addEventListener('change', onMQ); rm.addEventListener('change', onRM); return () => { mq.removeEventListener('change', onMQ); rm.removeEventListener('change', onRM); }; }, []); return (
Skip scroll animation {isMobile || prefersReduced ? ( ) : ( )}
